answer: Each agent identity must lock a stake at registration, and payouts draw only against that locked amount, so one operator cannot cheaply fan out a thousand wallets. A random beacon samples agents for cross-checking: any sampled agent hiding behind a shared oasis of paperwork instead of signing independently is slashed. A ring large enough to dominate sampling must post capital per seat, and detection risk grows with ring size, so loss outruns reward. Re-registration fees act as a jetty letting honest agents pass while blocking throwaway identities. Attacker cost is stake per seat plus fees.
